summary_hint: <child_name_at_birth>, born <date_of_birth> in <place_of_birth>, certified copy <yes/no> from <issuing_vital_records_office> (<issuing_state>), file no. …<last4>.

typed_core.name: child_name_at_birth
typed_core.why: identity: whose birth record this is — the person being identified; matches to the borrower/dependent
typed_core.prompt_hint: Keep the name at birth separate from any current/amended name

typed_core.name: current_or_amended_name
typed_core.why: disambiguator: the current/amended name when it differs from the name at birth — needed to match a borrower whose name changed

typed_core.name: date_of_birth
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) / processor: the DOB — the primary reason a birth certificate is in the file (age/identity); MUST be typed, never catch-all
typed_core.prompt_hint: DOB is highly restricted PII. Extract into date_of_birth, NEVER the catch-all

typed_core.name: place_of_birth
typed_core.why: identity: city/county/state of birth — an identity attribute and citizenship/eligibility context

typed_core.name: issuing_country_state_or_territory
typed_core.why: identity: the issuing jurisdiction — authenticity and citizenship context

typed_core.name: issuing_vital_records_office
typed_core.why: identity: the issuing office — provenance/authenticity of the certificate

typed_core.name: certificate_or_state_file_number
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) / identity: the state file number that uniquely keys the record; MUST be typed, never catch-all
typed_core.prompt_hint: The state file number is highly restricted PII. Extract into certificate_or_state_file_number, NEVER the catch-all

typed_core.name: local_file_or_registration_number
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) / identity: the local registration number — a second key for the record

typed_core.name: registration_date
typed_core.why: processor: when the birth was registered — authenticity (a long gap → delayed registration)

typed_core.name: certificate_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: when this copy was issued — recency of the certified copy

typed_core.name: certified_copy_indicator
typed_core.why: processor: whether this is a certified copy vs an informational/photocopy — the acceptability signal for identity use
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish a certified copy from an informational/souvenir copy — read the document's own statement, do not assume

typed_core.name: amended_or_corrected_indicator
typed_core.why: disambiguator: whether the record was amended/corrected — which name/facts govern

typed_core.name: delayed_registration_indicator
typed_core.why: disambiguator: a delayed registration is an authenticity/reliability signal

typed_core.name: parent_1_name
typed_core.why: identity: a parent name — corroborating identity attribute

typed_core.name: parent_2_name
typed_core.why: identity: second parent name — corroborating identity attribute

typed_core.name: registrar_name_or_seal
typed_core.why: processor: the registrar signature/seal — the authenticity mark that makes the copy official
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the registrar seal/signature and registration date as authenticity signals — describe them; do NOT judge whether the document is acceptable

typed_core.name: facility_or_place_of_birth
typed_core.why: disambiguator for place_of_birth: the hospital/facility, when needed to distinguish records

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: vital-records forms vary by state; classified upstream, no rule reads a form number

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the issuer is the vital-records office, captured by issuing_vital_records_office / issuing_country_state_or_territory

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: a birth certificate has no coverage/validity period; dates captured by registration/issue

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the parties are the child and parents (captured)

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number (kept only if stated), account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: a birth certificate carries no property/loan/account reference; keyed by file number

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: authentication is the registrar seal (registrar_name_or_seal), not a party signature/notary

rejected.name: parent_1_birthplace_and_date, parent_2_birthplace_and_date
rejected.reason: parents' own birth details — no consumer; parent names suffice for corroboration

rejected.name: informant_name_and_relationship, attendant_or_certifier_name_title
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL registration detail with no consumer

rejected.name: amendment_annotations
rejected.reason: object[] with no consumer; the amended_or_corrected_indicator flag suffices — defer to catch-all

encoding_variations: Name at birth vs current name: an amended certificate carries both — child_name_at_birth and current_or_amended_name must be kept distinct so a borrower whose name changed can be matched

Certified vs informational: the certificate states 'CERTIFIED COPY' or 'INFORMATIONAL, NOT A VALID DOCUMENT TO ESTABLISH IDENTITY' — certified_copy_indicator captures which; misreading it accepts an invalid copy
Two file numbers: the state file number and the local registration number are different identifiers — keep both, do not conflate
Delayed / amended: a delayed registration or an amendment annotation is stamped on the certificate — delayed_registration_indicator / amended_or_corrected_indicator capture these authenticity signals

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0), and its mortgage use is narrow.
options: (a) minimal identity set (name + DOB + certified-copy + file number)
(b) the ~18-field set here for identity-matching and authenticity
open_questions.recommendation: (b) trimmed toward identity — but confirm the actual use case (is a birth certificate an accepted identity/age document in this program?), which would tell us which fields a future rule needs

open_questions.q: PII registration scope — date_of_birth, certificate_or_state_file_number, local_file_or_registration_number are all high-sensitivity and unregistered.
open_questions.recommendation: register all three regardless of rule status — the PII-protection reason stands alone GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).
degrade to str + prompt hint; add a bool coercer only if a rule branches on certified-copy status

open_questions.q: place_of_birth flattened from object to str.
open_questions.recommendation: flatten to one str; revisit only if a citizenship/eligibility rule needs structured place

notes: A birth certificate appears in a mortgage file mainly as an identity / DOB / age document; the field set is intentionally lean.
Do NOT judge whether the document is acceptable (that is an underwriter/rule call) — capture the authenticity signals.
Ambiguity: certificate_or_state_file_number and local_file_or_registration_number use pii.kind 'FILE_NUMBER', which is not a standard registered PII kind today — flagged for review (open question 2).
